[[Green Party of England and Wales|Green]] | after_party = [[No overall control]] }} The '''2024 Hastings Borough Council election''' was held on Thursday 2 May 2024, alongside the [[2024 United Kingdom local elections|other local elections in the United Kingdom]] being held on the same day. Half of the 32 members of [[Hastings Borough Council]] in [[East Sussex]] were elected. The council remained under [[no overall control]], but the [[Green Party of England and Wales|Green Party]] made significant gains in their number of seats, becoming the largest party on the council. The [[Conservative Party (UK)| Conservatives]] performed poorly, losing a third of their 2023 share of the vote and half their seats. [[Reform UK]] also lost their only seat, which they had gained in May 2023 following a Conservative Councillor switching parties.{{cite news |last1=Oxburgh |first1=Huw |title=Ex-Conservative councillor in Hastings joins Reform UK Party |url=https://www.sussexexpress.co.uk/news/politics/ex-conservative-councillor-in-hastings-joins-reform-uk-party-4141065 |access-date=4 April 2024 |work=Sussex World |date=12 May 2023}} The Labour group leader, Heather Bishop, lost her seat.{{cite news |last1=Oxburgh |first1=Huw |title=Hastings Borough Council election results 2024 - council remains in no overall control |url=https://www.sussexexpress.co.uk/news/people/hastings-borough-council-election-results-2024-council-remains-in-no-overall-control-4616300 |access-date=3 July 2024 |work=Sussex World |date=3 May 2024}} Prior to the election, the council was being run by a minority coalition of the Green Party and the subset of the independent councillors known as the 'Hastings Independent Group'.{{cite news |last1=Wright |first1=Charlotte |last2=Lee |first2=Shola |title=Hastings Borough Council: Leader and five other councillors quit Labour |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-sussex-67726989 |access-date=12 May 2024 |work=[[BBC News Online]] |date=15 December 2023}} Following the election a Green minority administration formed instead.{{cite news |last1=McLaughlin |first1=Paul |title=Green takeover, independents frozen out |url=https://www.hastingsindependentpress.co.uk/articles/news/green-takeover-independents-frozen-out/ |access-date=3 July 2024 |work=Hastings Independent |date=5 June 2024}} ==Background== Hastings historically been controlled by all 3 major parties. The [[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservatives]] first won a majority in [[1976 Hastings Borough Council election|1976]], but lost the council to [[no overall control]] in [[1980 Hastings Borough Council election|1980]].{{cite web |title=Hastings Borough Council Election Results 1973-2012 |url=https://www.electionscentre.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2015/06/Hastings-1973-2012.pdf |website=Elections Centre |access-date=4 April 2024}} The [[Liberal Democrats (UK)|Liberal Democrats]] won control in [[1996 Hastings Borough Council election|1996]], with the Conservatives having lost all their seats on the council the previous year. The [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour Party]] won control of the council 2 years later, and held a majority until [[2002 Hastings Borough Council election|2002]], with the Conservatives retaking the council in [[2006 Hastings Borough Council election|2006]]. Labour gained the council in [[2010 Hastings Borough Council election|2010]],{{cite news |title=Election 2010 {{!}} Hastings council |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/shared/election2010/council/html/3702.stm |access-date=4 April 2024 |work=BBC News}} and controlled the council until [[2022 Hastings Borough Council election|2022]].{{cite news |title=Sussex election results 2022: Labour wins control of Worthing for first time |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-england-sussex-61334904 |access-date=4 April 2024 |work=BBC News |date=6 May 2022}} In 2022, Labour won 9 seats (down 3) with 42.1% of the vote, the Conservatives won 4 with 29.6%, and the [[Green Party of England and Wales|Green Party]] won 3 (up 3) with 23.5%. Following this election, Labour formed a majority coalition with the Green Party, but later formed a minority administration after the Greens withdrew from the coalition.{{cite news |last1=Oxburgh |first1=Huw |title=Labour has new cabinet at Hastings Borough Council after split with Greens |url=https://www.sussexexpress.co.uk/news/politics/labour-has-new-cabinet-at-hastings-borough-council-after-split-with-greens-3889201 |access-date=4 April 2024 |work=Sussex World |date=21 October 2022}} Labour lost their position as the largest group on the council in December 2023, after the resignation of 8 councillors from Labour and the suspension of another.{{cite news |last1=Connelley |first1=Chris |title=Coalition Cabinet draws fire from Labour and Tories |url=https://hastingsonlinetimes.co.uk/hot-topics/politics/coalition-cabinet-draws-fire-from-labour-and-tories |access-date=4 April 2024 |work=Hastings Online Times |date=21 January 2024}} A minority coalition of the Green Party and the 8 who left Labour was then formed, with a Green Party leader. The seats up for election in 2024 were last contested in [[2021 Hastings Borough Council election|2021]]; because of the delay of all local elections due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom|COVID-19 pandemic]], the seats are up for election after 3 years rather than the usual 4.
